_validation_note: The 14-day window (May 24–June 7, 2026) produced zero survivors. The window was broadened to 21 days (May 17–June 7, 2026) per protocol. The broadened window also produced zero survivors. Every serious candidate failed at least one gate as follows. C_V1 (BEAD Subgrant Execution Stack): Gate 1 FAIL — the two confirmed in-window news articles (KUCB May 27, Alaska Public Media June 1) cover GCI's Aleutian cable outage and satellite backup service; neither article mentions BEAD, the Alaska Broadband Office, Thomas Lochner, or subgrantee grant agreements. The connection is inferential, not direct implication. Gate 3 additional FAIL — Layer 2 (NIST Notice of Award Amendment) controlling actor is unnamed in any fetchable primary source; Thomas Lochner as ABO Director appears only via an email address in an image-heavy PDF, not in a statute, org chart, or agency page that formally designates him as director; Layer 5 (THPO veto authority) is not documented in the ABO agency page that was successfully fetched. C_CS2 (Doyon CEO Transition Stack): Gate 1 FAIL on two counts — the Doyon CEO announcement was published March 9, 2026 (90 days outside the broadened window), and the source is a corporate newsroom page, not an independent news outlet. No independent news outlet covered the Winkelman appointment or the Doyon fiber project in the May 17–June 7 window. The Doyon April 2026 project update confirms the ADNR river easement was already granted in late summer 2025, removing the BLM/ADNR layer as a live decision point. Gate 5 additional FAIL — Winkelman's individual binary authority (vs. board vote) to authorize the July 2026 Yukon River cable-laying is not documented in any fetchable primary source. C_R1 (NRC Part 57 Microreactor Licensing Stack): Gate 1 FAIL — the primary trigger (POWER Magazine April 27, 2026) is 41 days before June 7, outside even the 21-day broadened window. The June 5 Antares Mark-0 criticality article is in-window but does not mention Alaska, Eielson AFB, or NRC Part 57. Gate 3 additional FAIL — the Orrick LLP analysis URL (L2 primary source) returns 404; the NRC OAR agency page returns 404; the Alaska DEC siting permit page does not name a specific controlling official. Gate 5 additional FAIL — Alaska DEC Layer (L4) does not name a specific official for the siting permit decision. C_F1 (Quintillion Nome-Homer Express): Gate 1 FAIL — the Alaska Public Media May 26 article (STAK AI data center) does not mention Quintillion fiber. Gate 3 FAIL — FCC DA-26-324 PDF is unreadable in binary form; FCC docket page returns 503; FCC cable landing license transfer application for GCI-Quintillion had not appeared in the IBFS database as of scouting. C_F2/C_CS1 (NANA Regional Broadband Network): Gate 1 FAIL — news trigger is an April 16, 2026 government press release (52 days outside broadened window, not an independent news outlet). Gate 3 FAIL — NANA board page returns 403; NANA Drake acquisition page returns 403; USACE poa.usace.army.mil returns 403. L3, L4, and L5 controlling actors cannot be verified. C_F3 (GCI-Quintillion Consolidation): Gate 1 FAIL, trigger outside any window. C_V2 (CMS Rural Health RHTP): Gate 1 FAIL, agency page not independent outlet, confirmed in prior run. C_V3 (GSA OASIS+ ANC 8(a) On-Ramp): Gate 5 FAIL (PCO unnamed); Gate 7 risk (SBA 8(a) recent repeat). C_CS3 (BSNC NHO Portfolio): Gate 7 FAIL (same SBA 8(a) layer chain as May 25, 2026 anatomy). C_R2 (DAF Enhanced Use Lease): Gate 1 FAIL, ADN May 5 trigger is outside broadened window, confirmed failure across multiple prior runs. C_R3 (USACE NWP 39/Section 404 STAK): Gate 5 FAIL (USACE Alaska District Commander not publicly named, poa.usace.army.mil returns 403); Gate 7 risk (STAK project already anatomized May 30). No mechanism survived both the 14-day and 21-day windows with all seven gates intact.
